key: Ask how far the atypical cells climb and whether the lesion is still mainly a viral infection: atypia in the lower third with koilocytes is low grade, while atypia reaching two-thirds or more, with block p16 staining, is high grade.
items: CIN 1 is the histologic equivalent of LSIL, with atypia limited to the lower third of the epithelium.
Koilocytes show productive viral replication in maturing cells, the typical picture of a low-grade lesion.
Atypia limited to the lower third
Surface cells still mature normally, so the lesion is graded low and usually regresses.
Most low-grade lesions clear as the immune system controls the virus, so they are watched.
Low-grade lesions are followed with repeat HPV-based testing rather than excised.
Wart-like cytopathic change reflects an infection making new virus, not a transformed clone.
Atypia reaching the surface with no maturation defines CIN 3, which is grouped as HSIL.
Carcinoma in situ is full-thickness atypia above an intact basement membrane, part of HSIL.
Continuous p16 shows that E7 has disabled Rb, which upgrades a borderline CIN 2 to HSIL.
Atypical cells reaching two-thirds of the thickness define CIN 2, a high-grade lesion.
Treated by LEEP or cone excision
High-grade lesions carry a real risk of progression, so the transformation zone is excised.
Small cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio
Immature cells with scant cytoplasm on cytology are the hallmark of a high-grade smear.
